questions.question: What is 'dice reasoning' primarily about?
options: Calculating the volume of a cube
Determining hidden, opposite, or adjacent faces of a die from one or more given views
Measuring the physical weight of a die
Drawing a new die from scratch
questions.rationale: Dice reasoning problems ask you to determine hidden, opposite, or adjacent face relationships of a die, based on one or more given views of it.

questions.question: How many faces does a standard cube (die) have?
questions.rationale: A standard cube has 6 faces, conventionally numbered 1 through 6 on a typical die.

questions.question: How many faces meet at any single vertex (corner) of a cube?
questions.rationale: Exactly 3 faces meet at each corner of a cube, forming the basis of the three-face corner rule.

questions.question: What does 'adjacency' mean for two faces of a die?
options: The two faces are opposite each other
The two faces share a common edge
The two faces have the same number
The two faces are never visible together
questions.rationale: Two faces are adjacent if they share a common edge — as opposed to being opposite, where they share no edge or vertex at all.

questions.question: What is the 'opposite face rule'?
options: Every face has two opposite faces
Each face of a cube has exactly one face directly opposite to it, and the two never touch or appear together in the same view
Opposite faces are always adjacent
A cube has no opposite faces
questions.rationale: Each of a cube's 6 faces pairs with exactly one other face directly across from it — the two opposite faces never share an edge and never both appear in a single view.

questions.question: Why do opposite faces of a die never touch?
options: They actually can touch in some cases
Because they lie on parallel, non-adjacent sides of the cube, with no shared edge or vertex between them
Because they are always the same color
Because dice are hollow
questions.rationale: Opposite faces sit on parallel sides of the cube, geometrically separated with no shared edge or vertex connecting them.

questions.question: What does the 'three-face corner rule' describe?
options: That a cube has no corners
At any corner of a cube, exactly three mutually adjacent faces meet, and no two of those three can be opposite each other
That opposite faces meet at every corner
That only two faces ever meet at a corner
questions.rationale: At each of a cube's corners, exactly three faces meet, and since opposite faces can never be adjacent, no two of those three can be an opposite pair.

questions.question: If two faces are seen together in the same view of a die, what does that tell you about their relationship?
options: They must be opposite faces
They cannot be opposite faces, since opposite faces never appear together in a single view
They must be the same face
Nothing can be concluded
questions.rationale: Since opposite faces never appear together in a single view, seeing two faces together immediately rules out the possibility that they are opposite each other.

questions.question: How many pairs of opposite faces does a standard cube have?
questions.rationale: With 6 faces pairing up into opposite pairs, a cube has 6 / 2 = 3 pairs of opposite faces.

questions.question: Why is memorizing the basic cube facts (6 faces, 3 per corner, 3 opposite pairs) considered essential before solving dice problems?
options: It isn't actually essential
Because these facts are used repeatedly as the foundation for every deduction in more advanced dice reasoning problems
Because exams only test these basic facts directly
Because dice reasoning doesn't build on these facts at all
questions.rationale: Every more advanced deduction in dice reasoning — adjacency checks, corner compatibility, rotations — relies on these basic cube facts as its foundation.
